title: He had everything… except peace.
paragraphs: A king with absolute power—undone by a single night he could not control.
You would think a man who rules nations could command his own mind.

And what looked like a small inconvenience…
was actually God interrupting history.
Let me pull you in closer.
Because this isn’t just about a king.
There are nights when your body is tired… but your soul is loud.

When your past whispers.
When your pride replays conversations.
When your secret sins sit beside your pillow.

You scroll.
You distract.
You numb.
“On that night the king could not sleep…” — Esther 6:1

While the king was awake…
a man named Haman was plotting death.

While the king was restless…
a righteous man named Mordecai remained unrewarded.

While the palace was quiet…
a nation stood on the edge of destruction.
God can use your discomfort to expose what your comfort has been hiding.
We label it stress… anxiety… inconvenience.
God is shaking something awake inside you?
Because the real tension isn’t just outside.
The silent king inside your chest.

“I’m fine.”
“I’m in control.”
“I don’t need God like that.”
Because no throne can quiet a soul that is disconnected from God.
“Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.” — Proverbs 16:18
Some scholars interpret the Book of Esther as a masterclass in divine providence—God working invisibly through ordinary events.

Your sleepless nights.
Your inner unrest.
Your quiet convictions.
It might not be your enemy.
Because here’s the truth we avoid:
It will tell you to ignore it.
A righteous act that had been ignored.
A wrong that needed to be made right.
The man marked for death was honored.
God can reverse what pride has distorted.
You and I are not just restless.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
Our pride separates us from God.
Our sin writes a verdict we cannot erase.
And no amount of control… success… or distraction can fix that.
Not as a king who couldn’t sleep…
…but as a Savior who chose not to escape suffering.
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
And He did not just expose the problem.
“He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree…” — 1 Peter 2:24
You don’t have to live restless anymore.
Not because your life becomes perfect.
But because your soul becomes anchored.
“Come to me, all who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.” — Matthew 11:28
Because the same God who used one sleepless night to save a nation…
Can use this moment to save you.
And receive what you cannot earn:
If this stirred something in you…
